title: Dynamic Reservoir Orchestration and Tenant Isolation PRD
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: PRD for Dynamic Reservoir Orchestration (DRO): a mechanism to flexibly allocate dormant reserved compute (reservoirs) to tenants for short bursts while preserving strict isolation guarantees and predictable SLA behavior. DRO aims to reduce tail latency and customer-perceived errors during transient load without violating reserved capacity commitments.
problem_statement: Customers with reserved dedicated capacity occasionally experience transient demand spikes that exceed their commit and cause either failed requests or costly fallbacks to lower-performing models or regions. Current mechanisms for burst are static (fixed burst credits, manual prewarm), offer poor observability, and risk cross-tenant interference. We need an automated, auditable, and safe orchestration layer that can temporarily provide extra throughput while ensuring tenants' reserved guarantees and platform SLOs.
goals: Enable automatic ephemeral allocation of idle reserved capacity (reservoirs) to tenants during short spikes (<= 120s)
Guarantee tenant isolation: no noisy-neighbor degradation of other tenants' reserved performance
Expose controls for tenant-configurable burst policies and admin guardrails
Provide telemetry and audit trails for every orchestration decision (who got what, why, and for how long)
Minimize changes required by runtime: DRO should integrate with existing autoscaler and routing policies
non_goals: Replacing long-term capacity planning or committed capacity contracts
Implementing tenant-to-tenant borrowing markets or chargeback accounting for this phase
Large-scale changes to model kernel selection or inference runtime core logic
constraints: Must respect existing SLAs for all reserved tenants; no measurable SLA degradation allowed
Operational surface must be deployable to Dedicated and Private control planes
Telemetry storage retention for DRO events limited to existing observability budget (30 days default)
No user-facing schema changes to Redwood API required for MVP
requirements: REQ-001: Discovery — System can detect candidate reservoir nodes with >= 30% unused headroom for the last 60s
REQ-002: Allocation — Controller can allocate up to N vGPU-equivalents from one or more reservoir nodes to an eligible tenant for a burst window (configurable per-tenant)
REQ-003: Isolation — Kernel-level cgroups or runtime QoS enforcement prevents reservoir allocations from causing >1% p99 latency regression on donor tenant's baseline workloads
REQ-004: Policy Engine — Tenant profile includes burst_enabled (bool), max_burst_capacity (vGPU equiv), burst_window_sec (int), and priority_tier (low/normal/high)
REQ-005: Observability — Each allocation emits an event with allocator_id, donor_nodes, capacity_given, start_ts, end_ts, reason_code, and request_trace_ids
REQ-006: Audit & Rollback — Platform operators can revoke allocations and trigger automatic rollback on policy violation or anomaly
REQ-007: Fallback — When DRO cannot satisfy allocation within 15s, requests are routed to configured fallback (standby model, regional fallback, or 429) as tenant configures
REQ-008: Cost Accounting — Track tokens and request counts served from reservoir allocations, surfaced in per-tenant billing reports (MVP: metering only, no chargeback)
REQ-009: Safety Limits — Global platform-level rate of reservoir usage must be capped and configurable per region and AZ
scope_changes: SC-001: Added explicit audit trail requirement after security review (was previously only advisory)
SC-002: Reduced ambition: MVP does not implement cross-tenant monetary chargeback; only metering for reporting
SC-003: Shifted runtime enforcement to existing cgroup/QoS primitives instead of modifying kernel scheduling to reduce rollout risk
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: In controlled load test, a tenant configured with burst_window_sec=60 and max_burst_capacity=4 vGPU-e receives allocations within 8s of spike start in >=95% of trials
AC-02: Donor tenant p99 latency measured over donor baseline workload shows <1% relative increase during simultaneous reservoir donations in all test permutations
AC-03: All DRO allocation events are visible in the Console Events timeline, with clickable links to request traces and allocation metadata
AC-04: Operators can manually revoke an active allocation from Console and the allocation terminates within 10s with a rollback event emitted
AC-05: If DRO cannot allocate within 15s, system triggers tenant-specific fallback route and records the fallback in telemetry
AC-06: Billing reports include a daily aggregate of tokens served from reservoir allocations for each tenant (MVP metering verified in sample billing export)
AC-07: End-to-end chaos test (node failure during donation) results in no data-plane correctness violations and has documented incident playbook steps
success_metrics: Reduce tenant-visible 429s during transient spikes by >=60% for tenants with burst_enabled=true
Maintain platform-wide reserved SLA compliance (uptime and p99 latency) at 99.95% during DRO-enabled experiments
Operator MTTR for resolving mis-allocations <15 minutes with audit evidence
Adoption: 25% of eligible dedicated customers opt into burst_enabled within 3 months of GA
design_considerations: Prefer soft preemption with graded throttles rather than hard eviction to reduce user-visible errors
Favor centralized policy engine with local decision hints at node agents to reduce allocation latency
Expose conservative defaults (max_burst_capacity <= 20% of tenant commit) and allow explicit opt-ins for aggressive profiles
Leverage existing telemetry pipeline (traces, events, metrics) to avoid new infra burden
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): Instrumentation and dry-run mode on staging for 2 weeks with simulated spikes
Phase 1 (Limited Beta): Enable DRO for up to 10 enterprise customers in one region with operator approvals
Phase 2 (Gradual GA): Expand to all Dedicated tenants over 6 weeks with feature flag and automated safety checks
Phase 3 (Private rollout): Provide on-prem package and ops-runbook for customers running Redwood Private
test_plan: Unit tests for controller logic and policy evaluation
Integration tests: node agent allocation + quota reconciliation
Performance: multi-tenant p99 latency matrix under donation load
Chaos: simulate donor node failure, network partitions, and operator revocation during active donations
Security: audit trail tamper-resistance test and RBAC validation
dependencies: ENG-91300: node agent QoS enforcement primitives
PM-520481: reserved capacity surface redesign (billing integrations)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cross-tenant interference causing SLA breaches. Mitigation: conservative allocation caps, preflight simulations, rollback hooks
Risk: Slow allocation path causing request timeouts. Mitigation: local agent hints + fail-fast fallback routing
Risk: Observability gaps. Mitigation: require schema-enforced event emission before allocation completes
notes: Security review scheduled 2025-03-18; added audit trail requirement after feedback
We defer chargeback/billing enforcement to Q3; MVP will surface metered data only
PM to run two customer design reviews before Beta: Tenant A (media company) and Tenant B (fintech)
